3.1.1.o: A governance structure for cyber security, set up and working, and endorsed by the board. Its purpose is to direct and control how the organisation approaches cyber security.
3.1.1.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.1.1.o: Set up a cyber security committee that the board has formally mandated.
3.1.1.1.a: Have the board pass a resolution that creates the committee and gives it its mandate.
3.1.1.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.1.r: Board resolution or minutes establishing the committee.

3.1.1.2.o: The committee is led by an independent senior manager who comes from a control function, such as risk or compliance.
3.1.1.2.a: Appoint the chair in writing, and record which control function they come from.
3.1.1.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.2.r: Appointment of the chair; the committee membership list.

3.1.1.3.o: The committee includes senior managers from all relevant departments (for example the COO, the CIO, the compliance officer and heads of business departments) and the CISO. Internal audit may attend, but only as an observer.
3.1.1.3.a: Name the members by role and by person in the charter, and check attendance against it.
3.1.1.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.3.r: Membership list in the charter; attendance records in the minutes.

3.1.1.4.o: A charter for the committee, written and approved, that sets out its objectives, its roles and responsibilities, the minimum number of members needed for a meeting, and how often it meets. It must meet at least once a quarter.
3.1.1.4.a: Draft the charter, have it approved, and schedule at least four meetings a year.
3.1.1.4.l3: The charter is approved and the committee meets at least quarterly, as it says.
3.1.1.4.r: The approved charter; minutes of every meeting, at least four a year.

3.1.1.5.o: Establish a dedicated cyber security function.
3.1.1.5.a: Set the function up with its own staff and mandate, and show it on the organisation chart.
3.1.1.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.5.r: Organisation chart; the function's mandate or terms of reference.

3.1.1.6.o: The cyber security function is independent of the IT function. To avoid conflicts of interest, the two have separate reporting lines, separate budgets and separate staff evaluations.
3.1.1.6.a: Check all three separately: who each function reports to, which budget pays for each, and who appraises each function's staff.
3.1.1.6.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.6.r: Organisation chart showing both reporting lines; separate budget lines; who carries out each function's staff appraisals.

3.1.1.7.o: The cyber security function reports directly to the CEO or managing director, or to the general manager of a control function.
3.1.1.7.a: Make the reporting line explicit in the organisation chart and in the CISO's job description.
3.1.1.7.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.7.r: Organisation chart; the CISO's job description.

3.1.1.8.o: A full-time senior manager leads the cyber security function. SAMA calls this person the CISO, and the role sits at senior management level.
3.1.1.8.a: Appoint the CISO in writing as a full-time role, at senior management grade.
3.1.1.8.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.1.9.o: The CISO must be a Saudi national and sufficiently qualified, and the organisation must obtain SAMA's no-objection before assigning the role.
3.1.1.9.a: Before appointing, confirm nationality and qualifications, and apply to SAMA for a no-objection. Do not appoint until SAMA replies.
3.1.1.9.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.9.r: SAMA's no-objection letter; the CISO's qualifications and experience on file.

3.1.1.10.o: The board allocates enough budget to carry out the cyber security activities the framework requires.
3.1.1.10.a: Present a cyber security budget to the board, tied to the strategy and the roadmap, and record the board's approval.
3.1.1.10.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.1.10.r: Approved cyber security budget; board minutes approving it.

3.1.2.o: A cyber security strategy that is aligned with the organisation's strategic objectives and with the banking sector's cyber security strategy, so that security initiatives and projects move the organisation where it needs to go.
3.1.2.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.2.e: Banks must align with the banking sector's cyber security strategy. For other member organisations, SAMA makes that alignment mandatory where it is applicable.

3.1.2.1.o: The cyber security strategy is written, approved, maintained and actually executed.
3.1.2.1.a: Write the strategy, have it approved, review it on a schedule, and track the initiatives it sets out.
3.1.2.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.2.1.r: The approved strategy with version history; progress reports on its initiatives.

3.1.2.2.o: The strategy is aligned with the organisation's overall objectives, with its legal and regulatory obligations, and with the banking sector's cyber security strategy.
3.1.2.2.a: Include a section in the strategy that shows each alignment explicitly.
3.1.2.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.2.2.r: The strategy, showing how it maps to business objectives, regulation and the sector strategy.

3.1.2.3.o: The strategy explains why cyber security matters to the organisation and what it brings, describes the future state the organisation wants to reach so it stays resilient to new threats, and sets out which initiatives and projects will get it there, and when.
3.1.2.3.a: Make sure the strategy contains all three: the case for security, the target state, and a dated roadmap of initiatives.
3.1.2.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.2.3.r: The strategy document and its roadmap.

3.1.3.o: A cyber security policy that is defined, approved and communicated, documenting the organisation's commitment to cyber security and its objectives.
3.1.3.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.3.1.o: The cyber security policy is written, approved and communicated.
3.1.3.1.a: Have the policy approved through the governance route in 3.1.4, then publish it and tell staff where it is.
3.1.3.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.3.1.r: The approved policy; evidence it was communicated, such as acknowledgements.

3.1.3.2.o: The policy is reviewed periodically, following a defined and structured review process.
3.1.3.2.a: Write down how and how often the policy is reviewed, and follow it.
3.1.3.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.3.2.r: Review procedure; records of each review and what changed.

3.1.3.3.o: The policy is an input to other corporate policies such as HR, finance and IT; is backed by detailed standards (for example a password standard or a firewall standard) and procedures; is based on best practice and national and international standards; and is communicated to the relevant stakeholders.
3.1.3.3.a: Cross-reference the policy from the HR, finance and IT policies, and list the supporting standards and procedures.
3.1.3.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.3.3.r: Other corporate policies referring to it; the list of supporting standards and procedures.

3.1.3.4.o: The policy includes: a definition of cyber security; the organisation's cyber security objectives and scope; a statement of the board's intent; general and specific responsibilities; references to the supporting standards and procedures; and requirements that information is classified by importance, protected in line with the risk appetite, has an owner, and is risk-assessed; that people are made aware of security and what is expected of them; that regulatory and contractual obligations are met; that breaches and suspected weaknesses are reported; and that cyber security is part of business continuity.
3.1.3.4.a: Check the policy against each of these items and add what is missing.
3.1.3.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.3.4.r: The policy, with each required item present.

3.1.4.o: Responsibilities for putting cyber security in place, keeping it working and promoting it are defined across the whole organisation, and everyone involved understands and takes on their part.
3.1.4.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.4.1.o: The board holds ultimate responsibility for cyber security. It makes sure there is enough budget, approves the committee charter, and endorses the cyber security governance, strategy and policy after the committee has approved them.
3.1.4.1.a: Put these duties in the board's terms of reference, and take each item to the board for endorsement.
3.1.4.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.4.1.r: Board terms of reference; board minutes endorsing the governance, strategy and policy and approving the charter and budget.

3.1.4.2.o: The cyber security committee monitors, reviews and communicates the risk appetite, periodically and whenever it changes materially; checks that the strategy supports the organisation's objectives; and approves, communicates, supports and monitors the governance, strategy and policy, the security programmes (such as awareness, data classification, data privacy and data leakage prevention), the risk management process, and the key risk and performance indicators.
3.1.4.2.a: Put these duties in the committee charter and plan the committee's agenda around them.
3.1.4.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.4.2.r: Committee charter; minutes showing each duty being carried out.

3.1.4.3.o: Senior management makes sure standards, processes and procedures reflect security requirements; that people accept and follow the policy, standards and procedures when they are issued or updated; and that security responsibilities are written into the job descriptions of key positions and of cyber security staff.
3.1.4.3.a: Assign each duty to a named senior manager, and update job descriptions.
3.1.4.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.4.3.r: Job descriptions with security duties; records of staff accepting policies.

3.1.4.4.o: The CISO develops and maintains the strategy, policy, architecture and risk management process; makes sure detailed standards and procedures exist and are in use; delivers risk-based solutions covering people, process and technology; develops the security team; oversees security activities across the organisation, including security monitoring (the SOC), compliance monitoring, incident investigations, threat intelligence and security reviews; carries out risk assessments of information assets; supports other functions with classification, project security requirements and reviews; runs the awareness programmes; and measures and reports key risk and performance indicators.
3.1.4.4.a: Write these into the CISO's job description and report on them to the committee.
3.1.4.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.4.4.r: CISO job description; reports to the committee covering these areas.

3.1.4.5.o: The internal audit function is responsible for performing cyber security audits.
3.1.4.5.a: Include cyber security audits in internal audit's charter and annual plan.
3.1.4.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.4.5.r: Internal audit charter; the audit plan; audit reports.

3.1.4.6.o: All staff are responsible for complying with the cyber security policy, standards and procedures.
3.1.4.6.a: Make compliance part of employment terms, and have staff acknowledge the policy.
3.1.4.6.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.5.o: Cyber security is part of project management and project governance, so that every project meets the organisation's security requirements.
3.1.5.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.5.1.o: Cyber security is part of the organisation's project management methodology, so that security risks are found and dealt with inside each project.
3.1.5.1.a: Add security steps and gates to the methodology document.
3.1.5.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.5.1.r: The project methodology showing its security steps.

3.1.5.2.o: The methodology makes sure that: security objectives are part of the project's objectives; the cyber security function is involved in every phase; a risk assessment at the start decides whether existing controls cover the requirements or new ones are needed; security risks go in the project risk register and are tracked; security responsibilities are assigned; and an independent party, internal or external, reviews the project's security.
3.1.5.2.a: For each project, check these six points at the right stage and record the result.
3.1.5.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.5.2.r: Project risk registers with security risks; start-of-project risk assessments; independent security review reports.

3.1.6.o: An awareness programme for staff, third parties and customers, building a culture where people make sound, risk-aware decisions that protect the organisation's information.
3.1.6.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.6.1.o: Awareness programmes are defined, approved and carried out, to raise awareness and build a positive security culture.
3.1.6.1.a: Write the programme for the year, have it approved, and deliver it.
3.1.6.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.6.1.r: The approved programme; records of what was delivered.

3.1.6.2.o: Awareness is provided to three audiences: the organisation's staff, its third parties, and its customers.
3.1.6.2.a: Plan activities for each audience separately.
3.1.6.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.6.2.r: The programme showing all three audiences; delivery records for each.

3.1.6.3.o: The programme targets security behaviours, tailored to the different audiences and delivered through multiple channels.
3.1.6.3.a: Choose content and channels per audience, such as e-learning, email, posters, the website and app messages.
3.1.6.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.6.3.r: Materials for each audience and channel.

3.1.6.4.o: Awareness activities happen periodically and throughout the year, not once.
3.1.6.4.a: Spread activities across the year in a calendar.
3.1.6.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.6.5.o: At a minimum, awareness explains the security measures in place, people's roles and responsibilities, and relevant new threats and events (for example spear-phishing and whaling).
3.1.6.5.a: Check the materials cover all three.
3.1.6.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.6.6.o: The programme is evaluated to measure how effective its activities are and to recommend improvements.
3.1.6.6.a: Measure results, for example phishing simulation rates or quiz scores, and record the improvements you make.
3.1.6.6.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.6.6.r: Effectiveness measurements; the recommendations and changes made.

3.1.6.7.o: Customer awareness covers both retail and commercial customers and, at a minimum, lists security measures customers can consider to reduce their own risk.
3.1.6.7.a: Publish customer guidance for both groups, with practical steps they can take.
3.1.6.7.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.6.7.r: Customer awareness materials for retail and commercial customers.

3.1.7.o: Staff are trained to operate the organisation's systems securely and to apply the security controls their roles require.
3.1.7.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.1.7.1.o: Staff receive specialist or security-related training suited to their job, including: people in key roles; the cyber security team; people who develop and technically maintain information assets; and people involved in risk assessments.
3.1.7.1.a: Identify each group, set the training each needs, and deliver it.
3.1.7.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.1.7.1.r: Training plan by role; attendance and completion records.

3.1.7.2.o: Staff are educated so they have the skills and knowledge to operate the organisation's information assets securely.
3.1.7.2.a: Include secure operation in induction and in role training.
3.1.7.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.1.o: A cyber security risk management process that is defined, approved and in use, and aligned with the organisation's enterprise risk management, so that risks to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets are properly managed.
3.2.1.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.1.1.o: The cyber security risk management process is defined, approved and implemented.
3.2.1.1.a: Write the process, have it approved, and use it.
3.2.1.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.1.1.r: The approved process; risk assessments carried out with it.

3.2.1.2.o: The process focuses on protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets.
3.2.1.2.a: Assess impact on all three in every assessment.
3.2.1.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.1.2.r: Risk assessments scoring each of the three.

3.2.1.3.o: The process is aligned with the organisation's existing enterprise risk management process.
3.2.1.3.a: Use the same scales, appetite and reporting as the enterprise process, or map to them.
3.2.1.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.1.3.r: The mapping between the two; cyber risks appearing in enterprise risk reports.

3.2.1.4.o: The process is documented and covers risk identification, risk analysis, risk response and risk monitoring and review.
3.2.1.4.a: Make sure the document describes each stage.
3.2.1.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.1.5.o: The process covers the organisation's information assets, including business processes, business applications and infrastructure components.
3.2.1.5.a: Assess risks at all three levels, not only for systems.
3.2.1.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.1.5.r: Risk assessments of processes, applications and infrastructure.

3.2.1.6.o: Risk management starts early in a project, before a critical change, when outsourcing is being considered, and when new products and technologies are launched.
3.2.1.6.a: Build these four triggers into project, change, outsourcing and product processes.
3.2.1.6.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.1.6.r: Risk assessments dated at each trigger.

3.2.1.7.o: Existing information assets are risk-assessed periodically, based on their classification or risk profile.
3.2.1.7.a: Set a reassessment frequency per classification and keep to it.
3.2.1.7.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.1.8.o: Risk activities involve business owners, IT specialists, cyber security specialists and representatives of key users.
3.2.1.8.a: Record who took part in each assessment.
3.2.1.8.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.1.9.o: Risk assessment results are reported to the relevant business owner, who is the risk owner.
3.2.1.9.a: Send each assessment to its risk owner.
3.2.1.9.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.1.9.r: Evidence each result was sent to its owner.

3.2.1.10.o: The risk owner accepts and endorses the risk assessment results.
3.2.1.10.a: Obtain the risk owner's sign-off on each assessment.
3.2.1.10.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.1.11.o: The organisation's cyber security risk appetite and risk tolerance are clearly defined and formally approved.
3.2.1.11.a: Write the appetite and tolerance statements and have them approved.
3.2.1.11.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.1.11.r: The approved risk appetite and tolerance statements.

3.2.2.o: A process to identify the cyber security implications of relevant regulations, communicate them, and comply with them.
3.2.2.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.2.1.o: A process ensures compliance with the regulatory requirements that affect cyber security across the organisation. It runs periodically and whenever new requirements take effect, involves representatives from key areas of the organisation, and leads to updates of the policy, standards and procedures where needed.
3.2.2.1.a: Keep a register of applicable regulations, review it on a schedule and when new rules arrive, and record the resulting policy changes.
3.2.2.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.2.1.r: Regulatory register; review records; resulting policy and procedure updates.

3.2.3.o: Compliance with the mandatory national and international industry standards.
3.2.3.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.3.e: Applies to banks. Other member organisations are excluded from this subdomain, except that if they store, process or transmit cardholder data, or use SWIFT services, they must implement PCI DSS or the SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework as relevant.

3.2.3.1.o: The organisation complies with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS), the EMV technical standard, and the SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework. SAMA's text names the SWIFT framework's March 2017 edition.
3.2.3.1.a: Confirm which of these apply to your business, and hold current evidence of compliance for each. Check SAMA's current expectation for the SWIFT framework version.
3.2.3.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.3.1.r: PCI DSS attestation; EMV compliance evidence; SWIFT attestation.
3.2.3.1.e: The framework was issued in 2017, and these standards have newer versions since. The current versions are what an assessor will usually expect.

3.2.4.o: Periodic reviews of the security of information assets, to check that controls are designed and implemented securely and that their effectiveness is being monitored.
3.2.4.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.4.1.o: Cyber security reviews are carried out periodically on critical information assets.
3.2.4.1.a: Set a review schedule for critical assets and keep to it.
3.2.4.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.4.2.o: Services used by customers or exposed to the internet are reviewed and penetration tested every year.
3.2.4.2.a: List these services and test each one at least annually.
3.2.4.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.4.2.r: Annual penetration test reports for each service.

3.2.4.3.o: Each review is recorded, including its results, the issues found and the recommended actions.
3.2.4.3.a: Use a standard review report format.
3.2.4.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.4.4.o: Review results are reported to the business owner.
3.2.4.4.a: Send each report to the owner of the asset reviewed.
3.2.4.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.4.4.r: Evidence each report reached its owner.

3.2.4.5.o: Follow-up reviews check that all issues found were addressed, that critical risks were treated effectively, and that agreed actions are being managed.
3.2.4.5.a: Track every finding to closure and re-check it.
3.2.4.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.4.5.r: Follow-up review records; the findings tracker.

3.2.5.o: Thorough, independent and regular audits of the security of information assets, carried out to generally accepted auditing standards and the SAMA framework, to give reasonable assurance that controls are well designed, implemented and monitored.
3.2.5.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.2.5.1.o: Cyber security audits are performed independently, in line with generally accepted auditing standards and the SAMA Cyber Security Framework.
3.2.5.1.a: Use auditors who are independent of what they audit, and audit against the framework.
3.2.5.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.5.1.r: Audit reports stating the standards and criteria used; auditor independence.

3.2.5.2.o: Cyber security audits are carried out according to the organisation's audit manual and audit plan.
3.2.5.2.a: Include cyber security in the audit plan, and follow the manual.
3.2.5.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.2.5.2.r: The audit plan; the audit manual; audit working papers.

3.3.1.o: Cyber security is built into human resources processes: staff agreements carry security responsibilities, and staff are screened before and during employment.
3.3.1.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.1.1.o: The human resources process defines, approves and implements cyber security requirements.
3.3.1.1.a: Write the security steps into HR procedures and have them approved.
3.3.1.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.1.1.r: Approved HR procedures containing the security requirements.

3.3.1.2.o: The effectiveness of the human resources process is monitored, measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.1.2.a: Track measures such as screening completed before start dates and access removed on leaving dates, and review them.
3.3.1.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.1.2.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.1.3.o: The HR process includes: security responsibilities and non-disclosure clauses in staff agreements, during and after employment; security awareness at the start of employment and during it; when disciplinary action applies; screening and background checks; and security steps when employment ends, such as revoking access and returning assets (badges, tokens, mobile devices and all electronic and physical information).
3.3.1.3.a: Check the HR process covers each item, and keep records per person.
3.3.1.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.1.3.r: Staff agreements with security and non-disclosure clauses; screening records; induction awareness records; leaver checklists showing access revoked and assets returned.

3.3.2.o: All facilities that host information assets are physically protected against deliberate and accidental security events, to prevent unauthorised physical access.
3.3.2.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.2.1.o: The physical security process is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.2.1.a: Write the physical security process, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.2.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.2.1.r: The approved physical security process; evidence it is in use.

3.3.2.2.o: The effectiveness of the physical security process is monitored, measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.2.2.a: Review entry logs, alarms and incidents against measures, on a schedule.
3.3.2.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.2.2.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.2.3.o: The physical security process includes, at least: entry controls, including for visitors; monitoring and surveillance (for example CCTV, GPS tracking of ATMs and sensors); protection of data centres and data rooms; environmental protection; and protection of information assets through their whole life, including transport and secure disposal.
3.3.2.3.a: Check each area is covered at every site that hosts information assets.
3.3.2.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.2.3.r: Access control and visitor records; CCTV coverage; data centre controls; environmental monitoring; transport and disposal records.

3.3.3.o: An asset management process that keeps one accurate, up-to-date register of all information assets and where they are, supporting finance, procurement, IT and security.
3.3.3.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.3.1.o: The asset management process is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.3.1.a: Write the asset management process, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.3.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.3.1.r: The approved asset management process; evidence it is in use.

3.3.3.2.o: The effectiveness of the asset management process is monitored, measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.3.2.a: Measure register accuracy, for example by reconciling it against discovery scans, and review the results.
3.3.3.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.3.2.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.3.3.o: The asset management process includes: one unified register; an owner and a custodian for each information asset; references to the other processes that depend on asset management; classification, labelling and handling of information; and discovery of new assets.
3.3.3.3.a: Keep a single register with owner, custodian and classification for every asset, and run regular discovery to find assets not yet in it.
3.3.3.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.3.3.r: The asset register; classification and handling rules; discovery results.

3.3.4.o: A cyber security architecture that sets out security requirements within the enterprise architecture and the design principles for building security, so security is strategic, consistent, cost-effective and end-to-end.
3.3.4.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.4.1.o: The cyber security architecture is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.4.1.a: Write the cyber security architecture, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.4.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.4.1.r: The approved cyber security architecture; evidence it is in use.

3.3.4.2.o: Compliance with the cyber security architecture is monitored.
3.3.4.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.4.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.4.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.4.3.o: The architecture includes: a strategic outline of security capabilities and controls based on business requirements; approval of the architecture; a requirement for qualified security architects; design principles for building controls and applying security requirements (security by design); and periodic review of the architecture.
3.3.4.3.a: Document the architecture with these parts, have it approved, and review it on a schedule.
3.3.4.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.4.3.r: The approved architecture; the architects' qualifications; review records.

3.3.5.o: Access to information assets is restricted to business need, on need-to-have and need-to-know principles, so only approved users get authorised and sufficient access.
3.3.5.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.5.1.o: The identity and access management policy, including responsibilities and accountabilities, is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.5.1.a: Write the policy with named responsibilities, have it approved, and apply it.
3.3.5.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.5.1.r: The approved policy; evidence it is applied.

3.3.5.2.o: Compliance with the identity and access management policy is monitored.
3.3.5.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.5.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.5.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.5.3.o: The effectiveness of the identity and access management controls is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.5.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.5.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.5.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.5.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.5.4.o: The policy includes: business requirements for access, on need-to-have and need-to-know; user access management for joiners, movers and leavers, covering every type of user, with staff changes started by HR and third-party changes started by the accountable party, requests formally approved, changes processed promptly, access reviewed periodically, and an audit trail of requests, approvals and revocations; automation to support access management; a centralised identity and access function; multi-factor authentication for sensitive and critical systems and profiles; and management of privileged and remote access, with multi-factor authentication for all remote access and, based on risk assessment, for privileged access to critical systems, periodic review of privileged and remote users, individual accountability, and controls on shared privileged accounts (limited and monitored, passwords kept confidential and changed often and at the end of each session).
3.3.5.4.a: Check the policy against each item. Evidence the key ones from the systems: MFA settings, access review sign-offs, and leaver removals matched to HR dates.
3.3.5.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.5.4.r: Access request and approval records; access review sign-offs; MFA coverage; privileged account list and reviews; shared account password records.

3.3.6.o: Security standards for application systems are defined, approved and implemented, compliance with them is monitored, and their effectiveness is evaluated.
3.3.6.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.6.1.o: The application security standard is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.6.1.a: Write the application security standard, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.6.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.6.1.r: The approved application security standard; evidence it is in use.

3.3.6.2.o: Compliance with the application security standard is monitored.
3.3.6.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.6.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.6.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.6.3.o: The effectiveness of the application security controls is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.6.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.6.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.6.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.6.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.6.4.o: Application development follows the approved secure system development life cycle (SDLC) methodology.
3.3.6.4.a: Write the secure SDLC, have it approved, and show each project following it.
3.3.6.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.6.4.r: The approved SDLC; project records showing its security steps.

3.3.6.5.o: The standard includes: secure coding standards; the security controls in place (for example configuration settings, which events to monitor and keep, including system access and data, and identity and access management); segregation of duties in the application, supported by a documented authorisation matrix; protection of data in line with its classification, including customer privacy; vulnerability and patch management; backup and recovery procedures; and periodic security compliance reviews.
3.3.6.5.a: Check the standard covers each item, per application.
3.3.6.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.6.5.r: The standard; authorisation matrices; patch records; backup and recovery tests; compliance review reports.

3.3.7.o: A change management process controls every change to information assets, with compliance monitored and effectiveness evaluated.
3.3.7.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.7.1.o: The change management process is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.7.1.a: Write the change management process, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.7.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.7.1.r: The approved change management process; evidence it is in use.

3.3.7.2.o: Compliance with the change management process is monitored.
3.3.7.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.7.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.7.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.7.3.o: The effectiveness of the security controls in change management is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.7.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.7.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.7.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.7.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.7.4.o: The process includes: security requirements for changes, such as impact assessment, classification of changes and review; security testing where applicable (penetration testing, code review of internally developed code, code review of external code where the source is available, or a code review report or independent assurance statement where it is not); approval by the business owner; approval by the cyber security function before the change goes to the Change Advisory Board (CAB); CAB approval; a post-implementation review of the security controls; segregation of development, test and production, both environments and people; a procedure for emergency changes; and fall-back and roll-back procedures.
3.3.7.4.a: Build each step into the change workflow, and sample changes to confirm they were followed.
3.3.7.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.7.4.r: Change records showing impact assessment, testing, business owner, security and CAB approvals, and post-implementation review; emergency change records; roll-back plans.

3.3.8.o: Security standards for infrastructure components are defined, approved and implemented, compliance with them is monitored, and their effectiveness is evaluated.
3.3.8.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.8.1.o: The infrastructure security standard is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.8.1.a: Write the infrastructure security standard, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.8.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.8.1.r: The approved infrastructure security standard; evidence it is in use.

3.3.8.2.o: Compliance with the infrastructure security standard is monitored.
3.3.8.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.8.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.8.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.8.3.o: The effectiveness of the infrastructure security controls is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.8.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.8.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.8.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.8.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.8.4.o: The infrastructure standards cover all infrastructure in the main data centres, the disaster recovery sites and office spaces.
3.3.8.4.a: Confirm the standards apply at every one of these locations.
3.3.8.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.8.4.r: The standards' scope; compliance results per location.

3.3.8.5.o: The standards cover every type of infrastructure, for example operating systems, servers, virtual machines, firewalls, network devices, intrusion detection and prevention, wireless networks, gateway and proxy servers, email gateways, external connections, databases, file shares, workstations, laptops, tablets, mobile devices and telephone systems.
3.3.8.5.a: Map each type in the asset register to the standard that covers it.
3.3.8.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.8.5.r: The mapping of asset types to standards.

3.3.8.6.o: The standard includes: the security controls in place (for example configuration settings, events to monitor and keep, data leakage prevention, identity and access management and remote maintenance); segregation of duties with a documented authorisation matrix; protection of data in line with its classification, including customer privacy; approved software and secure protocols; network segmentation; protection against malicious code, including application whitelisting and protection against advanced persistent threats; vulnerability and patch management; DDoS protection where applicable, using scrubbing services with an agreed bandwidth, 24x7 monitoring by the SOC, the service provider and the scrubbing provider, scrubbing tested at least twice a year, and protection for both main and disaster recovery sites; backup and recovery procedures; and periodic security compliance reviews.
3.3.8.6.a: Check the standard covers each item, and evidence the ones with numbers: DDoS scrubbing tests at least twice a year, and 24x7 monitoring.
3.3.8.6.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.8.6.r: Configuration baselines; segmentation diagrams; anti-malware and whitelisting coverage; patch records; DDoS contracts and twice-yearly test reports; backup tests; compliance review reports.

3.3.9.o: The use of cryptography is defined, approved and implemented, to protect access to and the integrity of sensitive information, and to confirm who sent a communication or transaction.
3.3.9.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.9.1.o: The cryptographic security standard is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.9.1.a: Write the cryptographic security standard, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.9.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.9.1.r: The approved cryptographic security standard; evidence it is in use.

3.3.9.2.o: Compliance with the cryptographic security standard is monitored.
3.3.9.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.9.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.9.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.9.3.o: The effectiveness of the cryptographic controls is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.9.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.9.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.9.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.9.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.9.4.o: The standard includes: the approved cryptographic solutions and any technical or legal restrictions on them; when each approved solution must be used; and management of encryption keys through their whole life, including archiving and recovery.
3.3.9.4.a: List approved algorithms and uses, and write the key management procedure.
3.3.9.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.9.4.r: The standard; key inventory; key lifecycle records.

3.3.10.o: Where personal devices are allowed for business use, that use is covered by an approved security standard, extra staff agreements and awareness training, so business information stays protected in storage and in transit.
3.3.10.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.10.1.o: The BYOD security standard is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.10.1.a: Write the BYOD security standard, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.10.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.10.1.r: The approved BYOD security standard; evidence it is in use.

3.3.10.2.o: Compliance with the BYOD security standard is monitored.
3.3.10.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.10.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.10.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.10.3.o: The effectiveness of the BYOD controls is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.10.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.10.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.10.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.10.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.10.4.o: The standard includes: the user's responsibilities, including awareness training; the restrictions and consequences for staff when security controls are applied to their devices, for example for modified (jailbroken) devices, when employment ends, or when a device is lost or stolen; separation of business and personal information, such as containerisation; rules for corporate apps and approved public apps; and mobile device management, with access controls on the device and the business container and encryption for storage and transmission.
3.3.10.4.a: If personal devices are not allowed at all, record that decision instead.
3.3.10.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.10.4.r: The standard; signed BYOD agreements; MDM enrolment and policy settings.
3.3.10.4.e: If personal devices are not allowed for business use, record that decision and the controls that enforce it.

3.3.11.o: Information assets are disposed of securely when no longer needed, so business, customer and other sensitive information cannot leak or be disclosed.
3.3.11.l3: Every control in this subdomain is at level 3 or above: defined and approved, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.11.1.o: The secure disposal standard and procedure is written, approved and put into practice.
3.3.11.1.a: Write the secure disposal standard and procedure, have it approved, and put it into use.
3.3.11.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.11.1.r: The approved secure disposal standard and procedure; evidence it is in use.

3.3.11.2.o: Compliance with the secure disposal standard and procedure is monitored.
3.3.11.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.11.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.11.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.11.3.o: The effectiveness of the secure disposal controls is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.11.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.11.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.11.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.11.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.11.4.o: Information assets are disposed of in line with legal and regulatory requirements when no longer needed, including data privacy rules.
3.3.11.4.a: Tie disposal to your retention schedule and to the privacy rules that apply.
3.3.11.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.3.11.5.o: Sensitive information is destroyed so it cannot be recovered, for example by secure erase, secure wiping, incineration or cross-cut shredding.
3.3.11.5.a: Specify the method per media type, and record each destruction.
3.3.11.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.11.5.r: Destruction certificates listing items or serial numbers, and the method used.

3.3.11.6.o: Third parties used for secure disposal, transport and storage comply with the disposal standard and procedure, and their effectiveness is periodically measured and evaluated.
3.3.11.6.a: Put the standard in their contracts, and check them periodically.
3.3.11.6.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.11.6.r: Contracts with disposal providers; certificates; periodic reviews of the providers.

3.3.12.1.o: A cyber security standard for payment systems is defined, approved, implemented and monitored, and its effectiveness is measured and periodically evaluated.

3.3.12.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.12.1.r: The approved standard; monitoring and evaluation records.
3.3.12.1.e: SAMA does not number the considerations for this subdomain; it refers to the SARIE and Mada documents instead. This item follows the subdomain's principle and those references.

3.3.12.2.o: For the Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express (SARIE), the framework refers to the SARIE Information Security Policy. SAMA's text names version 1.0, June 2016.
3.3.12.2.a: If you connect to SARIE, show compliance with the current SARIE security requirements.
3.3.12.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.12.2.r: Evidence of compliance with the SARIE security requirements.
3.3.12.2.e: SAMA does not number the considerations for this subdomain; it refers to the SARIE and Mada documents instead. This item follows the subdomain's principle and those references.

3.3.12.3.o: For Mada, the framework refers to the Mada Rules and Standards Technical Book: the security framework (Part IIIa), the HSM requirements (Part IIIb), and the SAMA CA IPK certificate procedures. SAMA's text names the 2016 editions.
3.3.12.3.a: If you participate in Mada, show compliance with the current editions of these documents.
3.3.12.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.12.3.r: Evidence of compliance with the Mada security framework, HSM requirements and certificate procedures.
3.3.12.3.e: SAMA does not number the considerations for this subdomain; it refers to the SARIE and Mada documents instead. This item follows the subdomain's principle and those references.

3.3.13.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.13.1.r: The approved electronic banking security standard; evidence it is in use.

3.3.13.2.o: Compliance with the electronic banking security standard is monitored.
3.3.13.2.a: Decide how compliance is checked and how often, and record each check.
3.3.13.2.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.13.2.r: Compliance check results; exceptions and what was done about them.

3.3.13.3.o: The effectiveness of the electronic banking security standard is measured and periodically evaluated.
3.3.13.3.a: Set measures that show whether the controls work, review them on a schedule, and record the improvements you make.
3.3.13.3.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.13.3.r: Effectiveness measures and trend reports; evaluation records; improvement actions.
3.3.13.3.e: Measuring and periodically evaluating effectiveness is how SAMA's maturity model describes level 4. It is still one of this subdomain's control considerations.

3.3.13.4.o: The standard covers four areas. Brand protection for online services, including social media. Online, mobile and phone banking: official app stores and websites; detecting and taking down malicious apps and sites; sandboxing; no caching of sensitive data; protection against man-in-the-middle attacks; multi-factor authentication at customer registration and for all services, with password-protected tokens, access revoked after three wrong passwords or PINs, mobile number changes only at a branch or ATM, requesting and activating MFA through different channels, and MFA for sign-on, adding or changing beneficiaries, adding utility and government payees, high-risk transactions over set limits, and password resets; adding and activating beneficiaries through different channels; high availability; telling SAMA and customers about scheduled downtime in good time; customer agreements setting out roles, responsibilities and liabilities; and SAMA's approval before launching a new electronic banking service. ATMs and point-of-sale terminals: preventing and detecting exploitation of their software and hardware (for example cables, USB ports and rebooting); hardening, malware protection, privacy screens, masking of passwords and account numbers on screen and receipt, geo-blocking (for example cards disabled by default outside the GCC, and magnetic stripe transactions disabled), CCTV, cards revoked after three wrong PINs, anti-skimming and PIN-pad protection; and stopping an ATM remotely if malicious activity is seen. SMS notifications: no sensitive data in messages (such as account balances, except for credit cards); alerts to both the old and new numbers when a mobile number changes; a message when a new MFA mechanism is requested; a message for every retail and personal financial transaction; and a message when beneficiaries are added, changed or activated.
3.3.13.4.a: Check the standard item by item, and evidence the specific rules from the live systems: MFA points, lockout after three attempts, SMS triggers, and SAMA approvals for new services.
3.3.13.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.13.4.r: The standard; MFA configuration; lockout settings; SMS notification rules; ATM hardening and anti-skimming records; SAMA approvals for new services; downtime notifications.

3.3.14.4.o: The process includes: a designated security monitoring team (a Security Operations Centre, SOC); skilled and continuously trained staff; a restricted area for SOC work; resources for monitoring 24x7; detection and handling of malicious code; detection and handling of suspicious events and anomalies; network packet analysis; well-protected logs; periodic compliance monitoring of application and infrastructure standards; automated, central analysis and correlation of logs (SIEM); reporting of security incidents; and independent periodic testing of the SOC's effectiveness, for example red teaming.
3.3.14.4.a: Check each item, and evidence 24x7 coverage and independent SOC testing specifically.
3.3.14.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.14.4.r: SOC charter and rota showing 24x7 cover; staff training records; SIEM use cases; log protection settings; red team or SOC test reports.
3.3.14.4.e: Banks: SAMA circular 29814/67 requires maturity level 4 for all components of this subdomain. Set the target to 4. Other member organisations: level 3 applies, unless SAMA has told you otherwise.

3.3.15.4.a: Check each item, and keep every incident in one repository.
3.3.15.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.3.15.4.r: Incident procedure; team roster and training; forensic retainer; incident repository; root-cause analyses; improvement reports to the committee.

3.3.15.7.o: After operations resume, the organisation sends SAMA IT Risk Supervision a formal incident report covering: the title; the classification (medium or high); when the incident happened and when it was detected; the information assets involved; technical details; root-cause analysis; corrective actions done and planned; the impact, such as data lost, services disrupted, data changed without authorisation, data leaked or customers affected; the total estimated cost of the incident; and the estimated cost of corrective actions.

3.4.1.o: Security controls are part of contract and vendor management, so security requirements are settled before a contract is signed and checked throughout its life.

3.4.1.1.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.

3.4.1.5.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.4.1.5.r: Procurement risk assessments; tender security requirements and evaluations; test results; incident escalation terms; exit terms; confidentiality agreements.

3.4.3.4.o: The policy requires: a risk assessment and due diligence on the provider and its services; SAMA's approval before using cloud services or signing with the provider; a contract with security requirements in place before use; data kept in Saudi Arabia in principle, with SAMA's explicit approval for any service outside it; no use of the organisation's data by the provider for other purposes; the provider implementing and monitoring the controls the risk assessment calls for; the organisation's data logically separated from other customers' and always identifiable; business continuity in line with the organisation's policy; the right to carry out security reviews, audits and examinations at the provider; and on exit, termination rights and the provider returning the data and then irreversibly deleting it.
3.4.3.4.a: Check each requirement for every hybrid or public cloud service before it is used.
3.4.3.4.l3: Defined and approved in writing, carried out in a structured way, shown with evidence, and checked for compliance.
3.4.3.4.r: Cloud risk assessments and due diligence; SAMA approvals; contracts with the required terms; data location evidence; exit and deletion terms.
